_schema.logs: one entry per log (a log = 1–2 weeks on one question, NOT one per small step); date = start YYYY-MM-DD (matches folder); optional updated = last change; status ∈ running|done|closed|blocked|failed; path relative to experiments/
_schema.note: Index pages render from this file, sorted by updated||date. Agents: prefer UPDATING the project's open log (bump updated, refresh tldr/status) over appending a new entry — see README.md 'Scope'.

dex-point-policy.title: Dexterous Point Policy
dex-point-policy.tagline: Point-cloud dexterous manipulation policy — ICLR 2027 resubmission workstream.

logs.title: Four poses cannot estimate a success rate
logs.tldr: The openarm-sim eval driver placed the object at the exact centre of its grid cell every episode, so a 512-episode run was four initial conditions repeated 128 times. Turning on 1 cm per-episode jitter moves the three-object mean by 0.3 points (23.2 -> 22.9%) and changes what every number means: cells had been saturating at 0/128 and 128/128, and the tennis ball scored 1.4% at the centre pose against 6.4% under jitter, a 4.6x per-object error. Re-ran the cross-hand table at 96 episodes per hand: Inspire 25.0% [17.4-34.5] vs Wuji and Sharpa 0/96 [0-3.85], now non-overlapping, with IK residuals reproducing the previous study to within a millimetre under completely different initial conditions. Checkpoint rule, launch cutoff and a paired McNemar analysis pre-registered before any eval ran.

logs.title: Rebuilding the object points beats the shipped pipeline; the contact-label winner flips by object
logs.tldr: Rebuilt DPP's object points (128 -> 2048 pts, mask erosion -> depth-gradient rejection, sensor-metric depth fusion) and trained two otherwise-identical finetunes that differ only in the contact label. Mean success_at_end over bottle/box/ball at 512 episodes each: learned-tactile label 36.8%, human label 31.7%, shipped 128-pt baseline 23.2%. The two labels trade places by object (human wins bottle 76.6 vs 49.0, loses box 14.6 vs 44.7 and ball 3.9 vs 16.6), and both checkpoints were selected on bottle alone, so no label claim survives. Measured why the labels differ at all: the human annotation is one grasp bit copied across five fingers (1.21 distinct finger columns of 5 over 69k frames, contact head 0.98 acc) while the learned tactile is a real 5-bit target (0.70). Also found the benchmark has four initial conditions, not 512 - the driver runs with zero position jitter.

logs.title: Handing the model the object doesn't fix the grasp
logs.tldr: 0/24 everywhere: three objects, every point density, both checkpoints, every training length, and with the contact grip enabled — while DPP is 7/24 in the same harness. Three diagnoses fell to measurement: the palm is not held rotated (it rotates, +56 deg/1000 steps vs DPP's -5), undertraining is refuted (18% better val bought no success and halved the reach), and grasp initiation is excluded (contact fires in 32% of chunks, nothing changes). Ships a measured metric-depth pipeline shared with DPP. CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (appended as section 10): the sim inputs were not at training parity, so two of this entry's exclusions do not hold. The '2048-point' object cloud carried only 403 distinct points padded with copies of one point (candidate pool never scaled past its 128-point default; 48000 candidates reaches true 2048), and the scene cloud was cap-bound and RANDOMLY decimated to 2.55 cm spacing over 363x163 cm versus training's uncapped 5871 points at 1.43 cm over 204x132 cm. Run forward on real held-out clips these same checkpoints reproduce 78-98% of true wrist motion (16.07 cm GT) but only 25-36% in sim, so the collapse is sim-input-side and the undertraining and palm-sweep readings are both withdrawn. All success_at_end numbers stand but are on the retired 4-initial-condition protocol. SECOND CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (section 11), and it goes to the premise: the object-conditioning network was NEVER TRAINED. Every weight sits at its initialisation to within weight-decay drift (point_mlp.0 expected 0.288675 vs observed 0.285176; out_proj 0.031250 vs 0.031192; LayerNorms 0.9974-0.9978 vs 1.0; lr*wd*steps predicts -0.2%), while the contact head in the same run trained normally. So the object points could not influence the output however good they were, which is also why 128 / 403 / 567 / 2048-distinct all gave identical behaviour. Additionally: every behaviour video published before 2026-07-31 filmed a DIFFERENT policy, because render_fail.sbatch never passed use_object_cond. And the reach itself was never object-relative. THIRD PASS same day: 'never travels to the bottle' is withdrawn as too strong - per-env instrumentation over 24 envs shows the wrist DOES close on the target (21.8 -> 13.2 cm). What actually happens is a STALL: the predicted closing rate decays monotonically toward zero (-5.47, -3.60, -1.78, -0.02 cm/chunk) and the fingertips never reach grasp range (best 12.3-15.5 cm), so the hand parks ~11-16 cm short and grips air. The decay replicates across two runs with identical inputs; the subsequent reversal does not, and is not claimed.

logs.title: Give the model the object — target-object cloud conditioning
logs.tldr: Adds a DPP-style per-object cloud (128 pts, PointNet) + object-name conditioning via the existing CLIP encoder to fix the palm-up grasp OOD; object cloud verified co-registered (chamfer 0 cm); 1.5 cm voxel validated; two-track 24 h run.

logs.title: Closed-loop sim eval — reach transfers, grasp pose doesn't
logs.tldr: Tier-0 sensible reach achieved after two deploy-side fixes; grasp 0/24 from a palm-up orientation collapse — model-level real→sim OOD, all deploy causes ruled out. CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (appended as section 08): this title is STRUCK IN BOTH HALVES. Tier-0 was never an object-relative measurement — it rested on a displacement magnitude (||wrist_end - wrist0||) that never referenced the object — and rendered object-relatively the hand never reaches GRASP RANGE: per-env instrumentation shows the wrist closing 21.8 -> 13.2 cm but the predicted closing rate decaying to zero (-5.47, -3.60, -1.78, -0.02 cm/chunk) and the fingertips stalling at 12.3-15.5 cm, so the hand parks ~11-16 cm short and the object never moves (obj_final_pos z=0.915, table height). The palm-up diagnosis also falls: neither policy controls palm orientation through the position-only 6-point IK (ours achieves -0.26 of command, DPP 0.000). The correct question is why the predicted trajectory is not aimed at the conditioned target object, which accounts for the grip firing in empty space, contact firing in 32% of chunks, and why six emulations of sim-input defects were all null.

logs.title: Contact generalizes to PnP/Tool; the 6-point abstraction breaks on hand scale
logs.tldr: Learned tactile-contact transfers to PnP (F1 0.70) and Tool (spray power-grip recovers ring+pinky; microwave's low F1 is a thumb-free GT artifact). DPP in the openarm-sim PnP benchmark scores 29.2% with Inspire (reproducing the ~27% baseline bit-for-bit) and 0/24 with both Wuji (20-DOF) and Sharpa (22-DOF) — the cause is finger reach, not DOF count: the retargeting IK displaces the wrist 2.8-5.4 cm. Rescaling fingertip targets fixes the IK and still scores 0/24, because DPP's input is six points too. Two earlier sim claims withdrawn; the debugging also found the bottle's object cloud smears past 30 cm on 14.2% of fine-tune frames (missing depth-gradient filter).
